short_title: Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers and Decimals
standard_text: Represent and solve problems involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 100 000, and of decimal numbers up to hundredths, using appropriate tools, strategies, and algorithms
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on adding and subtracting whole numbers to 100 000 and decimals to hundredths, matched to the Ontario curriculum: column addition with regrouping, subtracting across zeros, lining up decimal points, estimating to check, and money and race-time word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the places, then add or subtract from the right.
key_sub: Big numbers: ones under ones, and every 0 you regroup across becomes 9 (60 000 − 23 458 = 36 542). Decimals: line up the decimal points and write zeros (4.5 = 4.50, 10 = 10.00). Estimate to check: 4.5 + 2.37 is about 7, so the answer is 6.87, not 2.82.
body_html:
The idea: add and subtract the same places

Every digit has a place: ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones, tenths and hundredths. You can only add or subtract digits in the same place. When a place gets 10 or more, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tenths make 1 one, and so on.

Big numbers: line up the ones

Put ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on. Start on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Subtracting across zeros

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup from the next place. If that place is 0, go left to the first digit that is not 0. Every 0 you pass becomes 9.

Decimals: line up the decimal points

With decimals, line up the decimal points, not the last digits. Then tenths are under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. Write zeros so both numbers have the same number of places. A zero at the end does not change the value: 4.5 = 4.50.

Regrouping works the same way. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, and 10 tenths make 1 one, so a regrouped 1 can cross the decimal point.

Example

What is 4.78 + 2.56?

Hundredths: 8 + 6 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.

Answer: 7.34

To take a decimal from a whole number, write the whole number with a point and zeros: 10 = 10.00.

Estimate first, then check

Round each decimal to the nearest whole number and work it out in your head. 4.5 + 2.37 is about 5 + 2 = 7, so 6.87 makes sense and 2.82 does not. For big numbers, round to the nearest thousand: 45 678 + 28 547 is about 46 000 + 29 000 = 75 000. When you finish, check with the inverse: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits (4.5 + 2.37 = 2.82)Line up the decimal points. Write 4.5 as 4.50
Not regrouping (45 678 + 28 547 = 63 115)Write the regrouped 1 in the next column and add it in
Making each 0 into 10 instead of 9 (60 000 − 23 458 = 37 652)Each 0 you pass gives 1 away, so it becomes 9
Not writing the zeros (10 − 3.46 = 7.46)Write 10 as 10.00, then regroup to subtract
Forgetting the 1 that crosses the point (4.78 + 2.56 = 6.34)10 tenths make 1 one. Add the 1 to the ones

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about adding and subtracting in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum, Grade 5 students add and subtract whole numbers up to 100 000 and decimals to hundredths (expectation B2.4). They also estimate decimal sums and differences (B2.3) to check their answers.

faq.q: How do you add decimals with different numbers of decimal places?
faq.a: Line up the decimal points and write zeros in the empty places, then add from the right like whole numbers: 4.5 + 2.37 = 4.50 + 2.37 = 6.87.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 60 000 − 23 458?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and regroup from there; each 0 you pass becomes 9. 60 000 becomes 5 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 60 000 − 23 458 = 36 542.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: Estimate first by rounding (4.5 + 2.37 is about 7), then compare. After subtracting, add the answer to the number taken away: if 10 − 3.46 = 6.54, then 6.54 + 3.46 should give 10.

items.q: You add 45 386 + 2479 in columns. Which digit of 2479 goes under the 5 in 45 386?
items.e: The 5 in 45 386 is in the thousands place. Line up the ones on the right, so thousands sit under thousands: the thousands digit of 2479 is 2. (If you line up the numbers on the left, the 4 would go there, which is wrong.)

items.q: Sofia added 36 254 + 4718. She lined up the numbers on the left, not on the right, and got 83 434. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the ones on the right: 4718 has no ten thousands digit. Ones: 4 + 8 = 12. Write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 2 + 7 = 9. Thousands: 6 + 4 = 10. Write 0 and regroup 1 ten thousand. Ten thousands: 3 + 1 = 4. Answer: 40 972. Check: 40 972 − 4718 = 36 254.

items.q: To subtract 40 000 − 12 345, you must regroup across the zeros. What does 40 000 become?
c: 3 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 10 ones
4 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones
3 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones
3 ten thousands, 10 thousands, 10 hundreds, 10 tens, 10 ones
items.e: The ones need a regroup, but the tens, hundreds and thousands are 0. Go left to the 4 ten thousands and take 1: 4 becomes 3. Each 0 you pass gives 1 away to the right, so it becomes 9, and the ones get 10. Then 40 000 − 12 345 = 27 655.

items.q: Subtract. Regroup when the top digit is smaller.

items.q: Benjamin worked out 70 204 − 36 587 = 33 617. Which calculation checks his answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 33 617 + 36 587 = 70 204. You get back the starting number, so the answer is right.

sets.title: Add decimals: line up the decimal points

items.q: To add 6.4 + 3.25, you write 6.4 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 6.4?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 6.4 = 6 ones and 4 tenths = 6.40. 6.04 is wrong: it moves the 4 to the hundredths place.

items.q: Olivia lined up the last digits and got 3.89. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 6.40 + 3.25. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 2 = 6. Ones: 6 + 3 = 9. Answer: 9.65. Estimate: 6 + 3 = 9, so 3.89 is far too small.

items.q: To find 15 + 2.38, you can write 15 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 15?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 15 = 15.00. Then the 5 ones sit over the 2 ones: 15.00 + 2.38 = 17.38.

items.q: In 23.6 + 4.85, the decimal points are lined up. Which digit of 4.85 is under the 3?
items.e: The 3 in 23.6 is in the ones place. With the points lined up, ones sit under ones: the ones digit of 4.85 is 4. The 8 goes under the 6 (tenths), and the 5 has no digit above it.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 + 2 = 4. Ones: 7 + 4 = 11, write 11. Answer: 11.4. Check: 11.4 − 4.2 = 7.2.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 5.78 + 2.36?
items.e: 5.78 rounds to 6 and 2.36 rounds to 2. 6 + 2 = 8. The exact answer, 8.14, is close to 8.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 13.42 + 4.75?
items.e: 13.42 rounds to 13 and 4.75 rounds to 5. 13 + 5 = 18. The exact answer, 18.17, is close to 18.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 26.8 + 9.45?

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 6.8 + 4.75
items.e: 6.8 + 4.75 is about 7 + 5 = 12. Only 11.55 is close to 12. Check by working it out: Write 6.8 as 6.80. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, write 11. Answer: 11.55. Check: 11.55 − 4.75 = 6.8.

sets.title: Subtract decimals and estimate to check

items.q: To find 8 − 2.35, how should you write 8 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 8 is 8 ones, and its decimal point is after the 8. Write 8.00: two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 8.00 − 2.35 = 5.65.

items.q: Priya found 9.2 − 3.75 = 5.45. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 5.45 + 3.75 = 9.20 = 9.2. You get back the starting number, so her answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 6 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 16 − 9 = 7. Ones: 3 − 2 = 1. Answer: 1.7. Check: 1.7 + 2.9 = 4.6.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 9 = 3. Tenths: 8 − 4 = 4. Ones: 7 − 1 = 6. Answer: 6.43. Check: 6.43 + 1.49 = 7.92.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 13 − 4 = 9. Tenths: 6 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 16 − 7 = 9. Ones: 2 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 4 = 8. Answer: 8.99. Check: 8.99 + 4.74 = 13.73.

items.q: What is 8.6 − 1.09?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8.6 as 8.60. Hundredths: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 9 = 1. Tenths: 5 − 0 = 5. Ones: 8 − 1 = 7. Answer: 7.51. Check: 7.51 + 1.09 = 8.6.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 25.5 as 25.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 8 = 6. Ones: 4 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 18.65. Check: 18.65 + 6.85 = 25.5.

Line up the decimal points. Write 6.6 as 6.60. Hundredths: 5 − 0 = 5. Tenths: 7 − 6 = 1. Ones: 4 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: bring down 7. Answer: 78.15. Check: 78.15 + 6.6 = 84.75.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 11 − 4 = 7. Tenths: 4 − 4 = 0. Ones: 7 − 0 = 7. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 47.07. Check: 47.07 + 10.44 = 57.51.

Line up the decimal points. Write 33.1 as 33.10. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 0 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 7 = 3. Ones: 2 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 3 = 9. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 19.32. Check: 19.32 + 13.78 = 33.1.

items.q: What is 5 − 1.75?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 7 = 2. Ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 3.25. Check: 3.25 + 1.75 = 5.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 6 = 4. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 9 − 7 = 2. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 12.64. Check: 12.64 + 7.36 = 20.

items.q: What is 1 − 0.45?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1 as 1.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 0.45 = 1.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 30 as 30.0. Tenths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 2, each 0 becomes 9, and the tenths become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Ones: 9 − 2 = 7. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 17.2. Check: 17.2 + 12.8 = 30.

Line up the decimal points. Write 100 as 100.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 hundred: the hundreds become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 9 − 6 = 3. Tens: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 63.55. Check: 63.55 + 36.45 = 100.

items.q: Mateo worked out 12.4 − 5.75 and got 6.65. Use an estimate to check. What does the estimate show?
c: You cannot tell without working it out
items.e: 12.4 rounds to 12 and 5.75 rounds to 6, so the answer should be about 12 − 6 = 6. 6.65 is close to 6, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Arjun worked out 15.2 − 6.47 and got 11.27. Use an estimate to check. What does the estimate show?
c: You cannot tell without working it out
items.e: 15.2 rounds to 15 and 6.47 rounds to 6, so the answer should be about 15 − 6 = 9. 11.27 is much bigger than 9, so it is too big. Arjun probably took the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place. The correct answer is 8.73.

items.q: Emma worked out 18.6 − 4.35 on a calculator and got 22.95. Use an estimate to check. What does the estimate show?
c: You cannot tell without working it out
items.e: 18.6 rounds to 19 and 4.35 rounds to 4, so the answer should be about 19 − 4 = 15. 22.95 is much bigger than 15, so it is too big. Emma probably pressed + instead of −. The correct answer is 14.25.

items.q: Ethan worked out 7.25 − 3.8 and got 345. Use an estimate to check. What does the estimate show?
c: You cannot tell without working it out
items.e: 7.25 rounds to 7 and 3.8 rounds to 4, so the answer should be about 7 − 4 = 3. 345 is much bigger than 3, so it is too big. Ethan probably left out the decimal point. The correct answer is 3.45.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 14.3 − 5.68
items.e: 14.3 − 5.68 is about 14 − 6 = 8. Only 8.62 is close to 8. Check by working it out: Write 14.3 as 14.30. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 2 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 6 = 6. Ones: 3 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 13 − 5 = 8. Answer: 8.62. Check: 8.62 + 5.68 = 14.3.

sets.title: Word problems: money, race times and big numbers

items.q: At the sports store, Chloe buys a hockey stick for $34.99 and a roll of tape for $4.75. How much does she spend?
items.e: Put the two prices together: add. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 5 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 9 + 7 + 1 = 17, write 7 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 4 + 1 = 9. Tens: bring down 3. Answer: 39.74. Check: 39.74 − 4.75 = 34.99.

items.q: Leah pays for a $27.86 order at the bookstore with a $50 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Change is what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 50 as 50.00. Hundredths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 6 = 4. Tenths: 9 − 8 = 1. Ones: 9 − 7 = 2. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 22.14. Check: 22.14 + 27.86 = 50.

items.q: Winter boots cost $64.50 at one store and $48.95 at another. How much more do they cost at the first store?
items.e: How much more means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 64.5 as 64.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 9 = 5. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 4 = 1. Answer: 15.55. Check: 15.55 + 48.95 = 64.5.

items.q: There are no pennies in Canada, so a cash total is rounded to the nearest 5¢. Maya buys a sandwich for $4.37 and a juice for $2.85. She pays with cash. How much does she pay?
items.e: Step 1, add: $4.37 + $2.85. Hundredths: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 3 + 8 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Total: $7.22. Step 2, cash: $7.22 is 2¢ from $7.20 and 3¢ from $7.25, so she pays $7.20. ($7.22 is what a card would pay.)

items.q: Jayden has $40. He buys mitts for $12.45 and a toque for $9.80. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Step 1, money spent: $12.45 + $9.80 = $22.25. Step 2, money left: $40.00 − $22.25 = $17.75. Check: $17.75 + $22.25 = $40.00. ($18.25 forgets to write $40 as $40.00 before subtracting.)

items.q: Amira has $20. She wants a book for $7.85, a puzzle for $6.40 and a card for $4.95. Round each price to the nearest dollar. About how much is the total, and does she have enough?
items.e: $7.85 rounds to $8, $6.40 rounds to $6 and $4.95 rounds to $5. $8 + $6 + $5 = $19, which is less than $20, so she has enough. (The exact total is $19.20.) $17 comes from dropping the cents instead of rounding.

items.q: At the track and field meet, Noah ran the 100 m in 15.42 seconds and Nathan ran it in 14.87 seconds. How many seconds faster was Nathan?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 7 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Ones: 4 − 4 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 14.87 = 15.42.

items.q: At a swim meet, Mei swam 50 m backstroke in 48.65 seconds. Last year her time was 52.3 seconds. By how many seconds did she improve?
items.e: The improvement is the difference between the two times: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 52.3 as 52.30. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 2 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 6 = 6. Ones: 1 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 11 − 8 = 3. Tens: 4 − 4 = 0. Answer: 3.65. Check: 3.65 + 48.65 = 52.3.

items.q: A 4 × 100 m relay team ran its four parts in 16.25 s, 15.8 s, 17.04 s and 15.36 s. What was the team’s total time?
items.e: Total means add all four parts. Line up the decimal points. Write 15.8 as 15.80. Hundredths: 5 + 0 + 4 + 6 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 2 + 8 + 0 + 3 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 6 + 5 + 7 + 5 + 1 = 24, write 4 and regroup 2 tens. Tens: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6. Answer: 64.45.

items.q: In a ski race, Hana finished the first run in 48.76 seconds and the second run in 51.39 seconds. What was her total time?
items.e: Total means add the two runs. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 6 + 9 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 100.15. Check: 100.15 − 51.39 = 48.76.

items.q: At the skating rink, Liam skated one lap in 43.9 seconds. Zoe took 45.08 seconds. How much longer did Zoe take?
items.e: How much longer means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 43.9 as 43.90. Hundredths: 8 − 0 = 8. Tenths: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 9 = 1. Ones: 4 − 3 = 1. Tens: 4 − 4 = 0. Answer: 1.18. Check: 1.18 + 43.9 = 45.08.

items.q: In the long jump, Lucas jumped 2.85 m. His second jump was 0.4 m longer. How long was the second jump?
items.e: Longer means more: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 0.4 as 0.40. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 0 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.25. Check: 3.25 − 0.4 = 2.85.

items.q: A family biked 12.75 km on a trail in the morning and 8.6 km in the afternoon. How far did they bike altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 8.6 as 8.60. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 21.35. Check: 21.35 − 8.6 = 12.75.

items.q: A hockey arena had 17 485 fans on Friday and 18 362 fans on Saturday. How many fans came on the two nights?
items.e: Put the two nights together: add. Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 8 + 6 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Thousands: 7 + 8 = 15. Write 5 and regroup 1 ten thousand. Ten thousands: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Answer: 35 847. Check: 35 847 − 18 362 = 17 485.

items.q: A food bank hopes to collect 50 000 cans of food this winter. So far it has 32 768 cans. How many more cans does it need?
items.e: Find what is still needed: subtract. Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 0 − 8. The tens, hundreds and thousands places are 0, so regroup 1 ten thousand. Each 0 you pass becomes 9. 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 9 − 6 = 3. Hundreds: 9 − 7 = 2. Thousands: 9 − 2 = 7. Ten thousands: 4 − 3 = 1. Answer: 17 232. Check: 17 232 + 32 768 = 50 000.

items.q: One town has 63 205 people. Another town has 47 890 people. How many more people live in the first town?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: subtract. Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 5 − 0 = 5. Tens: 0 − 9. Regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens: 10 − 9 = 1. Hundreds: 1 − 8. Regroup 1 thousand as 10 hundreds: 11 − 8 = 3. Thousands: 2 − 7. Regroup 1 ten thousand as 10 thousands: 12 − 7 = 5. Ten thousands: 5 − 4 = 1. Answer: 15 315. Check: 15 315 + 47 890 = 63 205.

items.q: A truck driver drove 38 476 km last year and 46 958 km this year. How far did the driver go in the two years?
items.e: Put the two years together: add. Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13. Write 3 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 9 + 1 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 8 + 6 + 1 = 15. Write 5 and regroup 1 ten thousand. Ten thousands: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. Answer: 85 434. Check: 85 434 − 46 958 = 38 476.

items.q: A stadium has 45 000 seats. For a soccer game, 28 754 adult tickets and 9386 student tickets were sold. How many seats are still empty?
A school collected 38 760 bottle caps last year and 24 395 this year. Round each number to the nearest thousand. About how many bottle caps is that altogether?
items.e: 38 760 rounds up to 39 000. 24 395 rounds down to 24 000. 39 000 + 24 000 = 63 000. (The exact total is 63 155, which is close.) 62 000 comes from cutting 38 760 down to 38 000 instead of rounding.

items.q: Aiden needs a 10 m rope for a canoe trip. He has a 3.65 m piece. What number goes in the box to show how many more metres he needs? 3.65 + ☐ = 10
items.e: Use subtraction: 10 − 3.65 = 10.00 − 3.65 = 6.35. Check: 3.65 + 6.35 = 10.00 = 10. (7.65 forgets to write the zeros: 10 − 3 = 7, then brings down .65. 13.65 adds instead of subtracting.)
